revision.text:
If you want to quickly try SMCube in simulation mode, you can do as follows, using the Digital Clock example. To do that, follow these steps: * open Scicoslab * give the command *: 
 cd "C:\Evidence\scicoslab-4.4.1\contrib\scicos_ee\examples\scicos_flex\SMCube\DigitalClock"
*: (please put the correct directory) * then the command *: 
scicos();
* open DigitalClock.cos * open the superblock * double click on the block names "SMCube mode_selector.xml" * choose "Properties", and set "Mode" to 1 (to say interactive simulation), press ok * close the superblock window * Menu Simulate, Run * two windows will appear: the Demo board simulator and the SMCube simulation window. * Press the play button on the SMCube simulation window to start the SMCube simulation * Then, press the first button on the left of the simulated Demo board. The selector state machine which is graphically simulated will change its status.

= How to simulate and then generating code from a Scicos diagram =
Note: The images showed below refer to the example for FLEX named <tt>DCmotor_Simulation.cos</tt> in the 'DCMotor' folder.
To simulate a diagram and then use the same diagram to generate code is advisable to proceed in this way. Create your diagram using a superblock that contains the diagram of your embedded application. Outside the superblock put your simulation blocks. To link the outer blocks with the inner blocks you can use <tt>Goto</tt> and <tt>From</tt> blocks. See the images below. [[File:sim_main.png|center|thumb|200px|Outer blocks.]] [[File:sim_block.png|center|thumb|200px|Inner blocks.]]
By clicking on Simulate menu and selecting Run you can start the simulation. In this case you obtain the graph showed below. [[File:sim_run.png|center|thumb|200px|To start the simulation.]] [[File:sim_results.png|center|thumb|200px|Results of the simulation.]]
To generate code there are two ways: #:Copy the superblock and create another diagram to be used for code generation. #:Remove <tt>Goto</tt> blocks and substitute <tt>From</tt> blocks with zero-constants source blocks. The second approach is showed in the images below. [[File:cg_main.png|center|thumb|200px|Outer blocks.]] [[File:cg_block.png|center|thumb|200px|Inner blocks.]]

== Update Eclipse plugins == To enable the updates of RT-Druid and its related distribution of Erika Enterprise select "Help -> Install New Software"
[[File:RT-druid.1.6.0-update.01.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows how to select the "New Install Software".]] In the "Install" window
[[File:RT-druid.1.6.0-update.02.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the Eclipse "Install" window.]]
select add and enter a reference name for the file repository (e.g. RT-Druid) and the link
http://download.tuxfamily.org/erika/webdownload/rtdruid_beta [[File:RT-druid.1.6.0-update.03.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the Eclipse "Add Repository" window with the correct parameters.]]
by selecting "Ok" you will be prompted with a new screen. You have to select all RT-Druid sources. To speedup the update process you can unselect the option "Contact all site during install to find required software".
[[File:RT-druid.1.6.0-update.04.png|center|thumb|200px|This screenshot shows the Eclipse "Install" window with the correct parameters.]] Along the update process you may be prompted for a "Security Warning" simply click on "Ok" to continue with the process. Finally please restart Eclipse when asked by the installer. == Upgrading issues == RT-Druid 1.5.1 and newer are able to handle all version of eclipse from 3.3, while versions before 1.5.1 works only with eclipse 3.3 and eclipse 3.4. Note that project created with eclipse 3.3 and 3.4 may have incompatibilities with the CDT present in the newer versions of eclipse. Moreover versions of RT-Druid older than 1.5 requires evidencedir\bin\mymake_cygwin.bat to run make through cygwin. This means that moving a project from an old installation to a new one "mymake_cygwin.bat" may not exist or be in another position. To reduce this problem, RT-Druid 1.5.1 (and later) generates an equivalent file (called mymake.bat) inside the project itself with the right content for windows and for linux. The easiest and safest way to update an old project to a new one, is to create a new project, move/copy all files in the new project and, if necessary, update project properties.

In this way you ask make_launcher.bat script to use your file. Note that ''{ProjDirPath}'' is a variable replaced by eclipse with the actual absolute path of the project.
We suggest to do it in this way, because it allow you to move the location of your project and even change OS, without any change but just recompiling it. * Note that ''Build command'' position may change a little on old version of eclipse. After this two steps, every time you build your project, your makefile file is used.

'''Project:''' Remote wireless control of an inverted pendulum
'''Details:''' Engineering and building the inverted pendulum mounted on a 2-wheeled robot. Has remote wireless control with the implementation of a real-time wireless communication protocol.
'''Contact:''' Stefano Stella
'''Web-site:''' -
'''Project:''' Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU)
'''Details:''' Sensors (accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer, GPS) are integrated and information are acquired and filtered.
'''Contact:''' Alberto Savioli
'''Web-site:''' -
'''Project:''' Multi-effect Audio Processor
'''Details:''' Audio signal acquisition and generation (interfacing with a DAC). Contains fully customizable real-time audio effects (compression, equalization, filtering, delay, ...)with programming of the effects chain from PC.
'''Contact:''' Simone Conso
'''Web-site:''' -
'''Project:''' Hardware-in-the-loop flying simulator
'''Details:''' Implementation of a trajectory planning and the robust control for an autonomous helicopter on a FLEX board. Physical system is simulated using a second board or a PC.;
'''Contact:''' Luigi Ventriglia
'''Web-site:''' -
'''Project:''' Force sensor acquisition for controlling a robot manipulator
'''Details:''' Analog signal is acquired from a ATI-MIO-16E-1 force sensor. All the 6 signals need to be sampled and combined, and the Comau SMART3-S2 robot manipulator will be driven by the force sensor.
'''Contact:''' Davide Cuppone
'''Web-site:''' -
'''Project:''' Autonomous Vehicles Platooning
'''Details:''' Engineering and building of 3-4 small autonomous 2-wheeled robots with DC motors, encoders and other sensors. Implementing a robust platooning control to guarantee the mutual distance during the coordinated motion.
'''Contact:''' Marco Della Vedova
'''Web-site:''' -
'''Project:''' Ball plate using an array of foto-sensors
'''Details:''' Engineering and building the ball plate and designing a daughter board with MUXes to access each single sensor (up to 60 sensor are used). Interfacing the set-up with a PC application.
'''Contact:''' Stefano Stella
'''Web-site:''' -
'''Project:''' Domotic Device
'''Details:''' Engineering and building of a domotic device to monitor the power consumed by an electrical load. Interfacing it with domitic buses like Konnex and X10 (for future development) and Implementation for real-time scheduling of electrical loads (final target).
'''Contact:''' Marco Della Vedova
'''Web-site:''' -
'''Project:''' Wireless broadcasting of audio signals
'''Details:''' Data acquiring from an analog/digital audio source. Compression and coding the same for wireless broadcasting. Data receiving and converting the same to analog/digital audio output.
'''Contact:''' Marco Ghibaudi
'''Web-site:''' -

'''On-going work at the [http://robot.unipv.it Robotics Laboratory], University of Pavia''' In sparse order: 1)
Ettore Di Palma is working to the interfacing of FLEX boards to current sensors from [http://www.lem.com/ LEM], aiming at the wireless monitoring of electric loads. Sensors currently adopted are the [http://www.lem.com/hq/en/component/option,com_catalog/task,displayserie/serie,AT/output_type,/ AT series] components AT 100 B10 and AT 50 B10. The interface to the FLEX is already working. We aim to integrate the monitoring system into a domotic system, probably based on the X10 technology. 2)
Daniele Caprini is working to the interfacing of FLEX boards to the [http://www.yamar.com/DCB500.html Yamar DCB500] powerline transceiver for automotive applications, which is a potential alternative to the standard CAN and LIN buses. We are testing the communication system on an ignition system for racing cars. 3)
Marco Ghibaudi is working on a wireless audio broadcasting application, using FLEX boards together with the [http://www.rfsolutions.co.uk/acatalog/EasyBee_Zigbee_Module.html EasyBee] ZigBee radio module. The application is based on FFT transforms, [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavelet_compression wavelet compression], and optimized coding to use, among the other features, custom fixed point math with the Microchip dsPIC. 4)
Marco Della Vedova is working on a multi-robot application where small mobile robots are moving in environments with obstacles. The FLEX board controls each robot, and has to drive an H bridge for controlling the two DC motors, sample encoders, and receive external information from the integrated [http://www.rfsolutions.co.uk/acatalog/EasyBee_Zigbee_Module.html EasyBee] module. Here a [http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kQYTDYYn3pE demo video] is available. 5)
Alberto Savioli is developing a 6 DOF [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inertial_Measurement_Unit Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU)], interfacing the FLEX board with a 3-axis accelerometer, 2 2-axis gyroscopes, a GPS receiver, a magnetometer and a temperature sensor. The sensor data fusion is done using a [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalman_filter Kalman filter] running on the Microchip dsPIC controller. For more information, please contact head researcher [http://robot.unipv.it/toolleeo Tullio Facchinetti].
Ongoing work in collaboration with Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna, Pisa-Italy on the [http://www.open-zb.net/ OpenZB protocol]

'''Project:''' Model based development of automotive applications based on Open Source Tools and Technologies.
'''Details:''' The objective is to set up a rigorous development cycle leveraging cheap technologies.
The architecture consists of three FLEX cards connected through a CAN bus.
The major issues are: * Modeling of the complex hybrid dynamics of the mechanical and electrical engine using SCICOS * Modeling and simulation of the control algorithms using SCICOS * Modeling of architectural aspects of the FLEX/Erika platform using a specialized SCICOS blockset * Automatic code generation from SCICOS blocks and configuration of the RTOS
